messages.subject: Re: Error message in lavaan
parts:
You don't seem to have an answer yet, so I'll have a go.

That's a really big model, and it's hard to identify where the problem might be. Identification can happen because your model is specified in such a way that it is not identified, or it can happen that that particular model is not identified for your data.

In addition, you're using meanstructure and WLSMV which add complications.

Things I'd try:

 - Use ML (or MLR) instead of WLSMV. See if that helps. 
 - Model one factor at a time.  Run a model with just:
    negaff =~ PI01_01 + PI04_19 + PI01_07 + PI03_25 + PI04_13 + PI03_31
        And see if that fits. Then do the next factor.
       If one of those models is not identified, you've found the problematic part of the model. Do the same thing with items - remove one item at a time, and see if that fixes the problem.
 - If all the single factor models fit, try adding them together one at a time. It might be a combination of two factors that is the problem.
